title: Light Travels in Straight Lines
subject: Physics
objective: You can hear a friend round a corner but not see them: sound bends, light travels in straight lines. We draw its path as a ray.

fill.q: In a uniform medium light travels in ____ lines.
A ray shows the path and ____ of light.
A bundle of rays is called a ____.
Sharp ____ are evidence that light travels in straight lines.

tf.q: Light bends around corners as easily as sound.
tf.explain: Light's wavelength is tiny, so it hardly bends.

tf.q: In the 3-card test, light passes only when the holes are in a line.
A ray is drawn as a line with an arrow.
Shadows form because light passes through opaque objects.

ar.explain: Rays cannot curve into the shadow; R explains A.

ar.a: Light bends round corners like sound.
ar.r: Light has a much shorter wavelength than sound.
ar.explain: A is false; R is true and is why light does not bend noticeably.

mcq.q: We hear but do not see around a corner because sound:

options: the path and direction of light

mcq.q: In the 3-card test, the candle is seen only when:

short.q: Describe the 3-card activity and its conclusion.
short.solution: Make holes in three cards and line them up between a candle and your eye. You see the flame only when the holes are in a straight line, so light travels in straight lines.

short.q: Why can we hear a person around a corner but not see them?
short.solution: Sound waves (about 1 m long) bend round the corner; light waves are far shorter than 0.001 mm, so they practically do not bend.

match.explain: Straight-line travel explains shadows and the 3-card test.
